title: Attention kernel compatibility catalog + canary CI harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible compatibility catalog that maps attention kernel binary variants (FlashAttention v2/v3 and vendor-specific fused kernels) to a compact set of production-representative model shapes and runtime conditions, and ship a lightweight canary CI harness that automatically detects functional regressions and statistically significant perf regressions on PRs and nightly runs.

Scope:
- Catalog: binary identifier, device architecture (A100-40/A100-80/H100), dtype (fp16, bf16, int8/quantized), common sequence lengths (64/128/512/1024/2048), batch sizes, kv-cache on/off, and common model layouts (causal vs encoder-decoder prefixes).
- Canary CI: deterministic microbench cases that exercise prefill and decode hot paths across sampled shapes; compute correctness diffs (reduction on attention outputs) and perf metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, memory high-water mark).
- Regression gating: fail PR or raise alert when: functional mismatch above tolerance (L2 diff > 1e-3 for fp16 on the sampled shapes), or perf regression > 7% median latency increase or p99 tail increase > 25% for more than 3 consecutive nightly runs.

Rationale and trade-offs: full exhaustive matrix is infeasible (combinatorial explosion). We will use a statistically principled sampling strategy: stratified sampling across sequence length buckets, batch sizes and dtype. For each binary we collect an empirical distribution of latency and tensor outputs on a small corpus of synthetic and real prompt shapes derived from production traces. This reduces test runtime while keeping signal for common regressions.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data collection job (already prototyped): run 72-hour offline collector to aggregate production shape histogram and identify top N representative shapes per tenant class. (Done: run completed 2026-03-11; output stored in perf-bucket under kernels/catalog/2026-03-11.csv)
2) Compatibility catalog format: CSV rows with fields [binary_sha, device, dtype, seq_len, batch, kv_mode, model_family_tag, observed_p50_ms, observed_p99_ms, output_checksum]. We will publish this to Confluence and a small artifact in the runtime repo for the CI harness to consume.
3) Canary harness: a pytest-based runner invoked by CI that pulls the catalog artifact, executes the sampled microbench cases inside a warm container (replicates kv cache warmup when prefill is required), captures outputs (FP16 compare to reference binary) and perf metrics, uploads results to perf-dashboard, and annotates PRs with a compact summary.
4) Alerting & rollout: integrate with perf-dashboard alert rules. For gating, new PRs must pass the canary suite when modifying kernels or kernel-selector code paths. Nightly runs compare across last good binary to auto-open regression tickets and assign to owners.

Acceptance criteria:
- Catalog generation pipeline that outputs a signed CSV consumed by CI (artifact URL in links).
- Canary CI added to runtime repo and executed for kernel changes; PR annotation with pass/fail + perf deltas.
- Regression thresholds implemented and validated with synthetic regressions.
- Documented rollback/fallback: when a regression is detected in canary, automatic CI will block merge and recommend fallback to last pinned kernel variant; on prod, routing policy must be able to route traffic to v2-based variant.

Risks and mitigations:
- Flaky comparisons due to non-deterministic RNG or memory layout differences. Mitigation: zero RNG in microbench, use deterministic seeds, run each case 3x and use median. Add tolerances to comparison and signal absolute failures separately.
- CI runtime explosion. Mitigation: sample ≤ 12 shapes per PR, run full suite nightly only.
- False positives on tail latency from noisy infra. Mitigation: require regression to be consistently observed across 3 runs or show effect size with confidence intervals.

Owners and reviewers:

- Reviewers: Linh Tran, Omar Chen

Artifacts and references: see links.

Next steps (short term):

- Add deterministic warmup sequences to replicate prefix-heavy prefill shapes (blocker: need small helper in runtime for kv warmup that doesn't require full model load).
- Draft PR for pytest harness and perf upload (target PR by 2026-03-16).
